label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Moved from Phibsborough to Drumcondra on Saturday 17 October with Kilbarrack Van Co. It was a two-bed flat, though most of the stuff was mine, and the new place is a fourth floor walk-up with no lift, so not an easy job. I'm giving four stars and I'd book them again, but I'll go through the good and the not so good, because I read a load of these myself before picking someone.

The basics first. I booked through their website and paid a €50 deposit by Revolut, all very straightforward. The quote was €340 for two lads and the van for up to four hours. Every other quote I got was €450 or more, so they were the best value I found by a good distance. The move took about three and a half hours.

Now the not so good. They were due at 9 and arrived at half 10. In fairness, I got a text at 8:40 to say the previous job had overrun, so I wasn't left wondering, but I was still sat on boxes with a cold coffee for an hour and a half. It wasn't the end of the world for me, as I had nobody waiting on me at either end. If you're on a tight handover with a landlord, though, or you have to be out by a certain time, it would be a real problem. I'd tell them that when you book and leave yourself a bit of a buffer.

Dessie, who runs it, knocked €40 off the bill afterwards because of the delay. I didn't ask him to, he just did it, and I thought that was decent of him. So I paid €300 in the end.

The other thing was that my brass floor lamp got a chip in the base. Everything else was wrapped in blankets and arrived without a mark on it, but the lamp went in bare. It was my nanny's, so I was a bit gutted. If you have anything sentimental or awkward, point it out before they start loading and ask for it to be wrapped. And wrap the lamps, lads.

Now the good, and there was plenty of it. The couch wouldn't go round the turn on the third floor and I had visions of it living on the landing forever. The younger of the two lads (Kev, I think) pulled an Allen key out of his pocket, had the legs off in a couple of minutes and it went straight in. They also put my bed back together without being asked, and took away a flat pack shelf I didn't want, which saved me working out how to get rid of it. All of that came up four flights of stairs, and still inside the time quoted.

So, overall: good lads, a fair price, and they sorted problems on the spot instead of standing around looking at them. The late start and the lamp are why it's four stars and not five, but the way the lateness was handled is a big part of why I'd still recommend them. If your timing is flexible and you flag the fragile stuff, I don't think you'll do better for the money in Dublin. I'd use them again for my next move.

I went with "Kev, I think" since you weren't sure of the name. Check it with Dessie before posting, or swap it for "the younger lad".
